messages:
priya-cust: Hey support — our webhook consumers started getting 429s right after a deployment. Traffic spiked from ~100/s to ~800/s for ~90s. Only requests using API key sk-ACME-12345 hit 429s, other keys fine. We're on project=project-42 under org=acme. Any hints?

maria-support: Thanks — can you share a sample request_id and any request headers you can capture? Also, are you routing through a proxy or cloud NAT?

priya-cust: Request IDs: req_20260317_01 (attached). Example headers we log: `Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME-12345`, `User-Agent: vendor-webhook/1.2`, `X-Real-IP: 10.0.0.7`, `X-Forwarded-For: 34.12.56.78`. We do sit behind Cloudflare + GCP NAT egress.

maria-support: Looking on our side for req_20260317_01 — I see a bunch of 429s with `limit_scope=org` and `quota_bucket=burst`. That's odd if only one key was affected. Pasting a trimmed log snippet:

```
time=2026-03-17T14:22:11Z request_id=req_20260317_01 auth.key=sk-ACME-12345 auth.project=project-42 status=429 limit_scope=org quota=3600/3600 burst_window=60
time=2026-03-17T14:22:11Z request_id=req_20260317_02 auth.key=sk-OTHER-999 auth.project=project-99 status=200 limit_scope=key quota=OK
```

maria-support: So the service attributed the hit to the org bucket for that key. We need to rule out header stripping or proxy reordering.

jon-eng: Quick background — our scoping precedence is supposed to be: api key -> project -> org -> ip. However, if the auth header is missing or not parsable, we fall back to IP-based heuristics and in some burst coalescing flows we aggregate to org-level bucket to avoid noisy neighbor. With a NATed egress, lots of clients share one IP so IP-bucket exhaustion can look like org exhaustion.

alex-sre: Also, one known edge case: some HTTP proxies (and misconfigured load balancers) will re-order headers so the first header encountered gets picked by our legacy parser. If the `Authorization` header appears after a `X-Api-Key` placeholder (or is chunked), we might not see the key and mark request as unauthenticated briefly. Combined with a short burst, that can push traffic into the org fallback path.

maria-support: Can you confirm whether your retries are re-sending auth headers? Some SDKs drop auth on TCP connection reuse for certain retry flows and our parser can see intermittent authenticated + unauthenticated requests that look like a burst from the same IP.

priya-cust: The vendor implementation does lightweight retries. I rotated the key earlier and that temporarily restored traffic for ~2 minutes, then 429s came back. We can run a capture if you want.

jon-eng: Helpful repro I ran from a GCP NAT box:
```
for i in $(seq 1 800); do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} - %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME-12345" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/webhook &
done
```
I saw ~6% 429s with response metadata: `scope=ip`, `affinity=null`, and a minority labelled `scope=org`. That pattern matches NAT + intermittent auth parsing.

alex-sre: Short-term mitigations: 1) if you can, pin requests to a different egress IP (avoid shared NAT), 2) use a rotated key per vendor cluster so one key can fail without shading others, 3) request Dedicated capacity / project pinning (we can pin project-42 to a quota). For long-term, we'll validate auth-parsing order and a patch to prefer explicit `Authorization` parsing always.

maria-support: Next steps for us: Priya, please attach a raw request dump (headers + body) and the egress IPs and timestamps for a failing window. We'll match against our logs and escalate to eng-runtime with a reproducible sample. If this is P0 for you, we can open a support escalation to get eng-oncall involved.

priya-cust: Sending dumps and NAT egress `34.12.56.78` now. This is high priority for us — can you also confirm whether `Authorization` header order could be causing the key to be ignored?

jon-eng: We'll run an internal spike to replay your exact header order and proxy chain. If we confirm parser-order bug, we'll fast-track a fix and mitigate with a config rollout.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: rollout/ingest-parser-fix started at 2026-03-17T14:30:05Z (canary at 10%).

maria-support: Thanks — we'll update the thread after the replay and the canary results. For now, we've given Priya a temporary dedicated key and suggested vendor-side retry backoff to rate-limit bursts. :thumbsup:
